message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, meaning it does not readily accept an electron) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| | Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (lightest element) |
| | Molar mass | 1.00794 g mol⁻¹ |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (121 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| | Critical temperature | 33.0 K |
| | Critical pressure | 12.8 bar |
| | Triple point | 13.99 K, 0.00022 bar |
| | Heat capacity (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (298 K) |
| | Enthalpy of formation (ΔHf°) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition for elemental H₂) |
| | Standard entropy (S°) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (298 K) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy (ΔGf°) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition for elemental H₂) |
| **Physical State & Behavior** | State at STP | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Solubility in water | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Poor (except in supercritical CO₂) |
| | Flame color | Blue (non-luminous) |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electrical conductivity | Very low in gaseous form; becomes conductive when ionized (plasma) |
| | Magnetic susceptibility | Diamagnetic (weakly repelled by magnetic fields) |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series (visible and UV) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (H₂) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂O₂, HCl, H₂SO₄, NH₃, CH₄, H₂O₂, HF, H₂S, etc. |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive with many metals (forming hydrides), oxidizes readily in presence of oxygen or air, reacts with halogens, acids, and bases. |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (donates H⁺) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺). |
| | Redox behavior | Can act as both reducing agent (e.g., in hydrogenation) and oxidizing agent (e.g., in combustion). |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds (H–H, H–C, H–O, H–N, etc.), ionic bonds (as hydride, H⁻). |
| | Isotopic effects | Deuterium and tritium exhibit kinetic isotope effects; used in tracer studies and nuclear fusion research. |
| **Special Notes** | Nuclear fusion potential | Tritium + deuterium → helium + neutron (energy release). |
| | Role in astrophysics | First element formed after Big Bang; abundant in stars; key in stellar nucleosynthesis. |
| | Environmental impact | Green fuel when produced via electrolysis; emits only water upon combustion. |
| | Safety considerations | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (1–4 % H₂ in air). Requires proper ventilation and explosion-proof equipment. |

---

### Quick Summary

- **Lightest element**: atomic mass ~1 u, density <0.1 g L⁻¹.
- **Highly reactive**: forms hydrides with metals, oxidizes with oxygen, reacts with acids and bases.
- **Common oxidation states**: +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (molecular H₂).
- **Key physical constants**: boiling point –253 °C, melting point –259 °C, critical point 33 K, critical pressure 12.8 bar.
- **Spectroscopy**: prominent Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series.
- **Applications**: fuel (hydrogen economy), industrial feedstock (ammonia, methanol), laboratory reagent, tracer studies, nuclear fusion research.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
